name: National Capitalism
summary: Business nationalism is a current of American right-wing thought that joins laissez-faire, anti-communist and anti-union capitalism to protectionism, sovereignty and opposition to supranational bodies. It presents domestic producers and workers as victims of internationalist corporate and political elites, often in populist language, and has allied with religious and cultural conservatives.
scope: The American business-nationalist tradition as described on Wikipedia: ultraconservative industrialists of the 1930s onward (the anti-New Deal NAM-style bloc, the Birch Society milieu) and its modern political voice, Pat Buchanan's economic nationalism (The Great Betrayal, 1990s campaigns). It does not cover Hamiltonian or Listian economic nationalism in general, or non-American national capitalisms. Many statements fall outside the sources, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Business nationalists opposed expansive welfare states and New Deal-style programmes, preferring limited or market-friendly support, so a state-guaranteed health system runs against their line.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The movement resisted state wage controls and regulation of business decisions, so a substantial statutory wage rise is something its industrialists would oppose.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Its laissez-faire strand wants government kept out of business decisions, though its protectionism qualifies this for trade, so it agrees at home but not without limits.

public-ownership.rationale: Defence of private enterprise against the state is the movement's founding motive, so public ownership of energy, rail and utilities is anathema.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The movement favours low taxes and low spending, and its industrialists fought tax rises on business and wealth.

unions-good.rationale: It backed union busting and the Taft-Hartley Act, though it has occasionally allied with unions on trade protection, which keeps this at disagree rather than strong disagree.

property-fundamental.rationale: Protection of property rights is one of the few state roles the movement explicitly demands.

regulate-corporations.rationale: It opposes regulation that limits business decisions, but its populism also attacks multinational corporate internationalists, so it rejects general tightening only moderately.

cut-welfare.rationale: It opposed expansive welfare and deficit-funded social programmes and wanted limited, contributory support, so cuts are in line even if few adherents use the dependency argument.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership by workers contradicts the producerist defence of owner-run enterprise and the movement's anti-socialist outlook.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents are wary of federal power (the Birch tradition) yet strongly anti-communist and hawkish on security; the sources do not address surveillance, so this is a genuine split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from its alignment with religious and cultural conservatism and family-values rhetoric; the sources do not discuss drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from its limited-government and anti-elite populism and the ties to conservative cultural movements; hate speech law is not discussed in the sources.

strong-leader.rationale: Buchanan ran on a leadership of conviction, but the Birch and business strands distrust concentrated federal power, so adherents are split; sources do not address bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement wants a government limited to protecting property, markets and strategic industries, not an end to the state, so it rejects the claim despite distrusting federal power.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from its limited-government, republican and conservative stance; gun control is not discussed in the sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communism, post-war support for military action and conservative law-and-order outlook; funding of police is not discussed directly.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with religious conservatives and family-values appeals; the sources do not discuss sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: It distrusts the federal government and invokes states' rights (via the Birch tradition) yet demands a strong national trade and sovereignty policy; inferred, adherents split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from conservative cultural alignment; criminal-justice philosophy is not covered by the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Buchanan stresses family values and community stability and has been tied to religious and cultural conservatism, which makes the family central.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Buchanan is described as opposing gay rights alongside abortion and secular humanism, and the movement allied with religious conservatives.

abortion-legal.rationale: Buchanan declared he would be the most pro-life president in history and wanted life constitutionally protected from conception.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement has allied with religiously conservative movements against secularism, and funders like J. Howard Pew backed evangelicals.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Buchanan opposed affirmative action and race-based preferences, and the movement's populism targets elite-driven social programmes.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its traditional family and cultural conservatism; the question is not addressed directly in the sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural nationalism and nativism are factions of the movement, and opposition to immigration bridges its economic and cultural nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: It resisted the New Deal as radical change and wants to preserve institutions, but Buchanan also demands sweeping reversal of trade policy; split, inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The movement's nativist wing and Buchanan call for closing the borders to immigrants, and opposition to immigration bridges its economic and cultural nationalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Buchanan opposes GATT, NAFTA and the WTO as continued surrender of national sovereignty, and the Birch tradition wanted the US out of the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Buchanan rejects free trade outright in The Great Betrayal and calls for a new nationalism, and the movement opposed GATT, WTO and NAFTA.

nation-first.rationale: America first is Buchanan's stated guiding principle, and the movement opposes corporate internationalists and global bodies.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Buchanan favours non-intervention unless vital US interests are involved, which excludes human-rights wars.

open-borders.rationale: Buchanan's message is to close the borders to immigrants, so open borders is the opposite of the position.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from its producerist industrial boosterism and hostility to regulation; environmental growth limits are not discussed in the sources.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to regulation of industry; climate is not addressed in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Industrial and manufacturing pride is central, but the sources do not discuss technology optimism; inferred, no clear position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from its support for domestic industry and energy producers such as the oil entrepreneurs it counted among backers; nuclear is not discussed.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement defends established property and the constitutional order and fought the New Deal by political means, so revolution is not part of it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Its populism and anti-elitist rhetoric cast experts and elites as out of touch, but the sources do not address expert policy-making directly; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The movement saw New Deal regulation and communism as threats to free enterprise, so planned economies are rejected on its core principles.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public or worker ownership of business conflicts with its defence of private enterprise against socialist and communist ideas.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred from its low-tax, pro-property stance; the specific tax is not discussed in the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Its low-tax, pro-property industrialists, many of them family firm owners, resisted heavy taxes on wealth; inheritance tax specifically is inferred.

basic-income.rationale: It opposed expansive welfare and wanted limited, contributory support, so unconditional cash for all adults is rejected.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Buchanan credits tariffs with making America an industrial power, and the movement supports tariffs, quotas and subsidies for domestic producers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: It wants protection of strategic industries but opposes government direction of business decisions, so adherents are split on state steering of investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Producerist rhetoric praises small business and domestic producers, but the industrialist core defends large firms; split, inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The movement's defining anti-communism and defence of free enterprise reject abolishing money and wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Money-power rhetoric in the movement's history targets bankers, but its main body is mainstream business conservative; the sources give no clear central-bank position.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: It backed business-led resistance to collective bargaining and state wage and price controls, so state-recognised bodies setting wages and prices conflict with its stance.

one-party-rule.rationale: It operates through electoral and lobbying politics within the US system and used right-wing populism, with no call for a single ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from its American republican setting (the Birch tradition insists the US is a republic); monarchy is not discussed.

democracy-best.rationale: The Birch tradition says the US is a republic, not a democracy, while Buchanan-style populism appeals to the people against elites; split, inferred.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from the Birch tradition's insistence on a constitutional republic; direct lawmaking is not discussed in the sources.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power are a communist idea that the movement exists to oppose.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from its national-sovereignty emphasis; secession is not addressed in the sources.

natural-rulers.rationale: Industrialist leaders saw themselves as the proper leaders of business-run politics, but its populist rhetoric rejects elites; split, inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Sources do not discuss this; the movement worked through political and lobbying means, though anti-communist rhetoric accepts force abroad; split, inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: Buchanan's non-interventionist America first line and the movement's isolationist origins make celebrating war unlikely; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement allied with religious conservatives against secularism, so strict separation is opposed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religious conservatives are allied with it but the sources do not show a demand that law follow scripture; split, inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: It wants government to protect property and defend the country, so private provision of defence is inferred to be rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Buchanan favours non-intervention but a strong defence of vital interests; superiority over rivals is inferred and adherents may differ.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The nativist and ethnocentric factions favour a national majority identity, but mainstream business nationalists avoid ethnic language; split, inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Adherents regard class-conflict doctrine as a communist idea and promote class cooperation under producerist rhetoric.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Its anti-New Deal, anti-union, anti-welfare outlook opposes redistribution toward equal results.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from its property-rights and sovereignty emphasis; the sources do not discuss indigenous peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from its America first, anti-foreign-aid stance; the question is not covered by sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to supranational bodies and its national sovereignty focus.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Laissez-faire business conservatism suggests this view, but the sources do not state it; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from its limited government and property-rights emphasis and the fact that sources never describe a communitarian duty doctrine.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from its industrial boosterism and anti-regulation stance; the sources do not discuss nature.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from its pro-life and family-values stance; population policy is not addressed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement celebrates industrial power: Buchanan credits protection with turning an agrarian republic into the leading industrial power.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred; the movement values manufacturing but defends established institutions, and the sources do not discuss accelerating disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from religious and cultural conservatism; not discussed in the sources.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of distant elites and government; not addressed in the sources.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources do not address this, and its anti-state and security-hawk strands pull opposite ways; split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Business nationalists framed the New Deal as a corruption of an earlier order and Buchanan stresses restoring earlier industrial strength; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is ideologically driven (radical anti-communism, laissez-faire); pragmatism over ideology is inferred to be disfavoured.

direct-action.rationale: It acts through lobbying, party politics and campaigns such as Buchanan's runs, so elections remain the channel; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: A purely philosophical statement the sources never touch; no clear stance.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement's identity is industrial and manufacturing pride, so a return to foraging is plainly rejected.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Producerist industrial capitalism rests on organised production and the wage system, so abolishing the division of labour is rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is the communist formula the movement opposes; it holds that rewards follow work and ownership.

production-for-use.rationale: Profit-driven private enterprise is the system it defends against communism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: It denies the Marxist labour theory, treating profit as the legitimate return to owners and producers, and cast class-conflict claims as communist.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Radical anti-communism is its central post-war cause, so proletarian dictatorship is the enemy position.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is a communist policy it opposes in defence of private property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The movement defends capitalism and saw its enemies as international finance and communism, not capitalism as the cause of war.

taxation-theft.rationale: It favours low taxes but wants the state to protect property and markets, and the sources never call taxation theft; split, inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with moral conservatives who support state action on morals; not addressed in sources.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Property rights are emphasised, but its populism speaks of nations and communities as well; sources do not settle it.

conscription.rationale: Sources do not address the draft; non-interventionist and libertarian strands oppose it while patriotic and security hawks accept it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from its national-sovereignty and republican emphasis; not discussed.

state-as-business.rationale: Business-run government appeals to industrialists, but its populism and national loyalty do not treat citizens as exit-ready customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Its opposition to the New Deal and welfare states rests on freedom as freedom from state interference with enterprise.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anti-elite populism and Birch-style distrust of establishment institutions suggest agreement, but the sources do not state it; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The racist faction would agree, mainstream business nationalists avoid the subject, and sources do not state a position; split.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from its partisan, electoral conduct; not discussed in the sources.

total-state.rationale: Opposition to direct government limits on business decisions and to state control of life is core, and fascist total-state ideas are not its programme.

national-rebirth.rationale: Producerist populism speaks of national industrial decline caused by elites and trade deals and seeks revival; rebirth language is inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Buchanan's America first favours non-intervention unless vital interests are involved, and the movement began isolationist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A feudal arrangement the sources never mention, plainly outside a modern capitalist movement.

bound-labor.rationale: A feudal institution never mentioned in the sources and inconsistent with its free-enterprise principles.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from conservative opposition to relativist ideas; not covered by the sources.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred from its Christian and cultural conservatism; the sources do not address it.

single-common-good.rationale: Sources never discuss this; industrialists and populists would differ on whether one common good exists.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Buchanan said Israel is well equipped to defend itself and he would not commit troops, while other adherents are more supportive; the right to a state itself is not stated.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from its restrictionism on immigration; not discussed directly.

revive-national-language.rationale: Irrelevant to its American context and not addressed in sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Business owners' control of enterprise was the point of the movement's resistance to unions and regulation.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from its conservative alignment and market-friendly approach; school policy is not covered by the sources.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The movement favoured low spending, opposed deficit-funded social programmes, and the NAM backed balanced budgets in the 1950s and 1960s.

economic-freedom.rationale: Its laissez-faire strand and fight against New Deal controls rest on the idea that political freedom needs free enterprise.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and an essentially Confucian idea outside the movement.

national-self-determination.rationale: Its sovereignty-first nationalism holds that nations should govern themselves free of supranational bodies, though self-determination as a general principle is inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: It opposes the UN and international organisations as surrender of sovereignty and Buchanan's America first has the US decide for itself on vital interests.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Inferred from its religious conservatism and opposition to secular humanism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Its nativist wing and its opposition to immigration put citizens first, and it opposed welfare broadly, so reserving what remains for citizens fits.

work-for-welfare.rationale: It preferred limited, contributory or market-friendly support, so a work requirement fits better than unconditional aid.

class-collaboration.rationale: Producerist rhetoric casts workers and owners as one nation of producers against elites and foreign interests, rejecting class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from its cultural conservatism and defence of heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred from its isolationism and non-alignment; a common front of dominated nations is not discussed.

workers-nation.rationale: It rallies workers behind national producers through trade protection, not an international class; this is the producerist logic of its populism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from its traditional family and religious conservatism; the sources do not discuss gender law.

ban-interest.rationale: Its defence of capitalism is incompatible with banning interest, though money-power rhetoric criticises bankers.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Its racist wing might favour it, but mainstream business nationalists did not make it a programme; sources do not state it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state is a communist idea; adherents treat the state as protector of property.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Backers included oil entrepreneurs such as J. Howard Pew and Clint Murchison, and the movement favoured domestic industry; expansion is inferred from that interest.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Its nativist and cultural-nationalist wing expects conformity to the national culture; assimilation as a demand is inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy rhetoric exists on the fringes, but mainstream adherents do not hold a replacement thesis; split, inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to the American constitutional system; not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Buchanan's non-interventionism rejects spreading American government abroad; the movement began isolationist.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from its traditional family and conservative alignment; not discussed in the sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Its populist, anti-elitist rhetoric casts political and corporate elites as out of touch and betraying workers.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from its pro-life and Christian conservatism; eugenics are not discussed in the sources.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from its pro-military and anti-communist outlook; not addressed in the sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Business nationalists want government to protect property, domestic markets and strategic industries, close to a limited state, though protectionism goes beyond the minimal one.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The racist faction might agree, but the sources do not document this as a movement position; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mainstream adherents would affirm equal rights, while its racist factions would not; split among strands.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialism is the enemy, and this is an internal communist debate that adherents reject in full.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from its American patriotism; not discussed in the sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from its national-unity and conservative stance; a religion-blind civil code is not discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from its American constitutional and religious context; not discussed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred; an Indian issue outside its American business setting, and the livestock and food industries are its constituents.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with religious conservatives and opposition to secular humanism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet doctrine on a socialist state; adherents oppose both the socialist state and state strengthening.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional republican tradition; the sources do not state it directly.

trade-surplus.rationale: Buchanan decries a record merchandise trade deficit and a swing from surplus to deficit with Mexico, so exporting more than importing is its goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Its nativist wing might favour restriction but pressuring a minority to leave is not documented as a position; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A strict non-aggression principle is libertarian, while adherents accept force against communism; split, inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Business competition is prized, but its protectionism limits competition between peoples; inferred, not stated.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Its radical anti-communism favoured suppression of communists, as in its overlap with McCarthyism; outlawing parties generally is inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican-theory concept the sources do not touch; its negative-liberty view makes it unlikely.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred from the Birch tradition's constitutional republic emphasis and fear of federal power.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine the movement opposes as part of its anti-communism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Its opposition to welfare and redistribution implies refusing first priority to the poor, though producerist rhetoric speaks for ordinary workers.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British issue; property-owner ideology favours it but the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: It backed the Taft-Hartley Act, which limited strikes, and opposed union protections generally.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Sources do not discuss poverty's causes; adherents would blame elites and trade more than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Opposition to immigration bridges economic and cultural nationalism, and the nativist wing holds this; the mainstream claim is inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to elections and the American republic; not discussed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Anti-communism produced support for suppression, while distrust of federal power opposes it; sources do not decide.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: It opposed wage controls and government limits on business decisions, so price fixing is rejected.

party-controls-media.rationale: It wants limited government and uses free-enterprise rhetoric, so state or party control of the media is rejected.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not discussed; incompatible with the American constitutional order it defends.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from its restrictionist position on immigration.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Industrialist backers see no case for it, though populism might favour it; inferred, not stated.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from its American constitutional tradition of independent legislators; not discussed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Buchanan calls NAFTA, GATT and WTO participation the continued surrender of American national sovereignty, rejecting pooling in principle.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from the American presidential system it works within; not discussed in the sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: A denominational matter the sources do not touch.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious conservatives are allied with it, but rule by clerics is not documented and conflicts with the American republic.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Radical anti-communism opposes revolutionary defeatism, a Leninist idea.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral conservatives favour it, while limited-government and business strands oppose censorship; split, inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from constitutional republicanism; not discussed.

recall-officials.rationale: Populist appeals favour it while constitutional conservatives are wary; not discussed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement began isolationist and Buchanan's America first limits involvement to vital interests, though anti-communism sustained alliances after the war.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from its property-rights stance; not discussed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not discussed; the movement favours military power and also an armed citizenry in some strands.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; its industrial and manufacturing orientation pulls the other way.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-elitist populism suggests agreement, but the statement is inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Its cultural nationalism and nativism treat the national culture as worth preserving over others; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from its conservative cultural alignment; not discussed in the sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with religious conservatives; not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious conservatives are allies, but the sources do not document a position; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from its family-values alignment; not discussed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Opposition to immigration suggests restriction, but birthright citizenship is not discussed in the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from its assimilationist and nativist wing; not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; religious conservatives in the movement would favour it.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from its cultural conservatism and emphasis on community stability.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: It opposes foreign aid completely and favours America first, so cancelling debts owed to rich-country lenders is rejected; inferred from that aid stance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed; an anti-colonial claim outside its setting.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to the existing constitution; not discussed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from its stress on liberty and free enterprise; not discussed.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Buchanan would end foreign aid completely, and the movement opposed foreign aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from America first sovereignty and a strong defence; not discussed directly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not discussed; the US president is chosen via an electoral college and the sources are silent.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Money-power rhetoric distrusts bankers, while business conservatives prefer stable money; not discussed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Buchanan opposes committing US troops for Israel, but the question concerns other countries' land; not addressed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property rights are treated as fundamental, which implies rejecting a common-good condition; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Adherents call the Soviet system communist and the enemy; whether it was state capitalist is a Marxist debate the sources do not touch.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to regulation of industry.

collective-defense.rationale: Anti-communist alliances were accepted after the war while Buchanan limits commitments to vital interests; split, inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with religious conservatives and distrust of state power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources never discuss a ceremonial head of state, and the American presidency it works within combines the roles.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; US-context nationalists may accept it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Alien to the American republican setting and not discussed; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Low taxes are preferred, but a flat rate is not discussed; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional-republic emphasis and fear of concentrated power.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, though the Birch tradition prizes a republic.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from its republican tradition; not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A communist internal debate the movement does not engage; rejected with socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizure of estates conflicts with its fundamental defence of property rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from its non-interventionism; not discussed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional American setting; not discussed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from its American setting; not discussed.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to supranational integration; not discussed directly.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its assimilationist, nativist wing.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the Marxist doctrine the movement opposes.

ban-cartels.rationale: Industrialists favoured business combination while populists attack corporate internationalists; not discussed directly.

no-bailouts.rationale: Free-enterprise principle suggests agreement but the sources do not state it and protected industries have sought help; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not discussed; populism and constitutionalism pull opposite ways.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from its traditional family and conservative alignment.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Buchanan's complaint that Americans no longer make everyday goods supports greater self-sufficiency, though a bloc shut off from trade is stronger than he states.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Buchanan's critique targets trade agreements themselves, not adding standards to them; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: A communist idea contrary to its profit-based enterprise.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A revolutionary-left doctrine alien to its constitutional, anti-communist politics.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Family firm owners favour inheritance rights, while populism attacks elites; not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural nationalism favours teaching national history; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Non-interventionism opposes ruling other societies; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from its cultural nationalism and American patriotism; school policy is not discussed directly.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Buchanan opposed affirmative action and race-based preferences, favouring excellence, ability, merit and character.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not discussed; money-power rhetoric might favour it but the mainstream business core opposes.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The movement defends capitalism and free enterprise against claims of its collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Non-interventionism makes this unlikely; not discussed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Business nationalists want protection of their own market, not de-linking by poor countries; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis the movement rejects; inferred from its opposition to communism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Property rights and free enterprise point to yes, while racism is an embarrassing faction; not discussed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional limits on government fit the Birch tradition, but the sources do not state it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the American republican setting.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred; not discussed in the sources.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the Birch tradition's constitutionalism and fear of federal tyranny.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Agricultural and industrial uses are accepted; inferred, not discussed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; industrialists funded evangelical causes but welfare is opposed.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Its leaders and businessmen funded organised political campaigns, so withdrawal is rejected; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School thesis the movement does not engage; inferred to be rejected with Marxist cultural theory.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis alien to the movement, which sees capitalists as legitimate leaders; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is a Marxist idea; inferred rejection, though the movement also claims foreign interests exploit American workers.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nativist wing might favour it; not documented as a mainstream position.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist question the movement does not address; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Buchanan would end foreign aid completely, which fits the view that poor countries should rely on their own resources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Non-interventionism opposes such demands; not discussed.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its nativist and property-rights stance; not discussed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from its conservative opposition to leftist political litmus tests; not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Its radical anti-communism treats communism as the main enemy; the equivalence is inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Buchanan's tariff history discusses the period only on trade.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its cultural conservatism and nationalism; not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from social conservative alignment; not discussed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Non-interventionism accepts that others govern themselves, but the sources do not address the claim.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional republic outlook, which keeps the military under civil control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to welfare and its traditional family stance.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from its family-values stress; not discussed directly.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its attachment to elections.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Buchanan and the movement want government to protect domestic markets and strategic industries from foreign interests.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from its family-values and religious conservative alignment; not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional republicanism; not discussed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The movement favoured a voluntary approach to Social Security and market-friendly support, so private accounts fit.

land-use-tenure.rationale: A defence of private property in land opposes tenure held only while used.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutional republicanism supports it; not discussed in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Cultural nationalism and nativism support a common national language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Its economic nationalism wants domestic markets and strategic assets protected from foreign interests; land ownership is inferred from that.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Buchanan opposed race-based preferences and held that judgments should rest on merit.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Business conservatives defend consumption and production; Buchanan's complaint concerns imports, not consumption itself.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anti-communism backed rollback, but non-interventionists oppose it; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Buchanan limits intervention to vital interests; not discussed directly.

corporate-influence.rationale: Populists criticise corporate fat cats and internationalists while industrialists lobby for protection; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to foreign and internationalist influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from family-values and anti-immigration positions; not discussed directly.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed; property-rights principle conflicts with the restriction.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort schemes conflict with its opposition to deficit-funded social programmes and to state intervention.

democratic-peace.rationale: Its non-interventionism rejects spreading democracy abroad; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from its respect for the constitutional order and law-and-order conservatism.

non-intervention.rationale: Buchanan holds America first non-intervention except for vital interests, and the movement turned to anti-communist interventionism after the war; split.

industrial-unions.rationale: It opposed collective bargaining protections, so organising form is inferred to matter little but unions are disfavoured.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The fringe of the movement promoted conspiracy theories about Jews and others, but mainstream adherents do not; split among strands.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from its family-values stance; not discussed.

local-production.rationale: Buchanan laments that Americans no longer make everyday goods, supporting domestic production; the local scale is inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: It worked through organised bodies such as the NAM and the Birch Society; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Buchanan calls participation in the WTO and similar bodies a surrender of sovereignty, and the Birch tradition opposed the UN.

religious-nation.rationale: Allied with religious conservatives, but the sources do not define the nation by religion; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its America first sovereignty; not discussed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: It defends private property of every kind, and this statement is the permissive part of what communists accept; agrees.

defeat-communism.rationale: Radical anti-communism is a defining element, with rollback favoured over containment after the war.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; market-friendly support suggests openness while public funding conflicts.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from its religious conservative alignment and its opposition to atheistic communism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The movement defends free enterprise as the engine of national prosperity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from its defence of the economic system and family stance; not discussed.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its traditional family stance and opposition to welfare.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not discussed; irrelevant to its American setting.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from its defence of private enterprise; not discussed.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its property and limited government outlook.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The movement defends laissez-faire capitalism and opposes communism, so a third course is rejected.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The racist fringe flirted with it, but mainstream adherents do not; not documented in the sources, so inferred from the movement's mainstream.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Buchanan opposed gay rights, but criminalisation is not documented as a position; inferred disagreement with the strongest form.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Anti-communist activism backed suppression of communists, but suppressing opposition generally conflicts with its liberty rhetoric; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from its American constitutional setting despite alliance with religious conservatives.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not discussed; its protectionist logic favours the home economy but the movement was isolationist.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic doctrine outside the movement; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from its American constitutionalism; not discussed.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from its republican emphasis, though populist appeals to ordinary people pull the other way.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from its conservative opposition to leftist social theory; not discussed directly.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to gay rights and conservative social views; not discussed directly.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from its strongly pro-life stance, which Buchanan holds from conception.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Business nationalism is firmly on the right; Buchanan's cross-class appeals blur lines, but it does not call the division obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept the movement rejects in defence of capitalist work and production.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Nativist wings may agree but sources do not document it; split, inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Religious conservatives are allies but the sources do not state this; split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from its religious conservative alliance.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to regulation on employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement rejects both laissez-faire-excluding social protection and state regulation; it fought New Deal-style regulation and welfare, so the combined model is disfavoured.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement is strongly anti-communist and hawkish about defence of vital interests, so abolishing armed forces is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Not discussed; industrialists accept inequality but its populism claims to defend workers.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement began isolationist but then backed anti-communist action after the war; split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from its American republican setting.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from its defence of private banking and capitalism.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sovereignty concerns favour refusing, but low spending favours austerity; split.

property-franchise.rationale: Business-run politics might favour it, but not discussed in the sources.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist thesis alien to its conservative outlook; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept the movement rejects; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A leftist criticism of capitalist freedoms; adherents reject it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Constitutional republic emphasis supports it; not directly stated in sources.

racial-franchise.rationale: The racist fringe might favour it, but it is not documented as the movement's position.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The antisemitic fringe might favour it, but mainstream adherents do not; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from its republican and electoral outlook.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with religious conservatives.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Its populists attack corporate internationalists, but business conservatives deny that wealth threatens liberty; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to gay rights and pro-military conservatism.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Atheism promotion is associated with communism, which it opposes, and it opposes secular humanism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its law-and-order conservatism and view that government protects property.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its nativist and majoritarian national outlook and American setting; consociational power sharing is not discussed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: It opposed expansive welfare and preferred voluntary approaches, and funders backed religious causes.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to representative republican institutions; liquid democracy is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with conservative evangelicals.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not discussed; traditional family stance suggests otherwise, but the sources do not say.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Its restrictionist and nativist views make non-citizen voting unwelcome.

rent-control.rationale: It opposes price controls and government limits on business decisions.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from its protection of property rights.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Isolationism favours withdrawal, while anti-communist strategy favoured bases; split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Profit and ownership income are what the movement defends against socialist critiques.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from its conservative defence of self-defence and arms.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its conservative alignment against feminist theory.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Anti-communism was cast as a struggle for civilization; the spiritual framing is not stated, so split.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from its religious conservative alliance.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with conservative religious movements.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Nativist wings favour this, while mainstream adherents defend free ownership; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions that exist should be independent of the state, but it opposed unions; inferred, low.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A leftist test of socialism that adherents do not apply; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership is rejected on principle, including utilities.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the American Congress it works within.

municipal-property.rationale: Common ownership of the means of production is rejected.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional republican emphasis; not discussed.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed; opposes wage controls but values family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to regulation of business.

person-over-state.rationale: Not discussed; individual liberty and national loyalty both appear.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from its religious conservative alliance.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Birch states' rights favours devolution, but sovereignty favours the nation; split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The racist fringe might agree but it is not mainstream; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not discussed; white nationalist supporters of Buchanan would agree, mainstream adherents typically avoid it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Buchanan's America first limits force to vital interests, and the movement began isolationist.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from its civic American setting.

free-public-college.rationale: It opposed expansive welfare and low-tax, low-spending conservatism rejects free tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to taxes and regulation on industry.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not discussed; traditional gender views suggest agreement.

arms-reduction.rationale: Strong defence outlook; not directly discussed.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic nationalism favours control, while free enterprise opposes; not discussed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from distrust of federal power and its conservative stance on arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: A Leninist anti-war idea alien to its patriotic anti-communism.

collective-bargaining.rationale: It opposed collective bargaining protections and union power.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Opposes deficit-funded social programmes; supplements are not discussed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: It favoured balanced budgets and opposed deficit-funded programmes.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from its America first stance, though it also wants trade rules changed in the US interest.

smash-state-machine.rationale: A revolutionary-left doctrine; adherents defend the constitutional order.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not discussed; patriotism strong but sacred language is not documented.

student-debt-relief.rationale: It opposes deficit-funded social programmes and spending.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from its religious conservative alliance.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from its low-spending and anti-elite stance.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with conservative Christians.

farm-price-support.rationale: Protectionist logic supports farm supports, but it opposes government price controls; split.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Strong defence outlook; not discussed directly.

workers-own-party.rationale: It is a business bloc fighting labour, and independent workers' parties are opposed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic-politics question the sources do not touch and that has no bearing on its American setting.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Property rights logic supports liability but regulation is opposed; not discussed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from its liberty and anti-regulation outlook.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Cultural nationalist wing favours this; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The movement backed Taft-Hartley and opposed union protections, including closed shops.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from its restrictionist, conservative position.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Birch tradition says the US is a republic, not a democracy; not directly stated.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its liberty and anti-government rhetoric.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Opposes welfare, but market-friendly support is acceptable; split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from American mainstream conservatism; not discussed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its alliance with religious conservatives.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to government growth.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: It opposes supranational bodies as surrender of sovereignty.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Evangelical allies would agree, but the sources do not state it; split.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defending planned states opposes the movement's anti-communism.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its electoral republic outlook.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist and assimilationist stance.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from its pro-industrial, pro-business outlook.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: Buchanan's nationalism and alliance with cultural conservatives treats the homeland as a heritage to be defended, though the sources do not use spiritual language.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the business-nationalist tradition stresses constitutional order and law-and-order, but the sources are silent on killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Buchanan's The Great Betrayal attacks trade deals and trade with low-wage countries such as China as ruinous to American workers.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: Buchanan's America-first line opposes foreign entanglements, which weighs against supporting kin minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is laissez-faire and property-centred, so it does not see natural resources as equally owned by all.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the strand's laissez-faire and anti-union capitalism emphasises individual property in labour and body, though it was not framed in those terms.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: Buchanan preferred tariff revenue to other taxes, but the sources give no stand on consumption taxes on everyday goods.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: the anti-welfare, laissez-faire strand favours limiting aid to the needy over broad universal programmes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: Buchanan campaigned within the Republican and Reform parties and the strand works through parties and business groups, though its rhetoric is populist.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: adherents are split between laissez-faire opposition to privileges and support for tariff protection of domestic producers.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the tradition has allied with religious conservatives, who do not object to religion shaping politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: the strand combines industrial capitalism with religious and cultural conservatism, which fits joining technology to inherited values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: its alliance with social conservatives suggests resistance to easy unilateral divorce, though the sources do not discuss it.

national-resource-control.rationale: Business nationalism stresses sovereignty and opposes supranational bodies, and Buchanan argues for national control of the economy.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Business nationalists defend laissez-faire and reject redistribution, so they hold that wealth is just if earned by market process regardless of equality.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Business nationalists oppose new taxes and internationalist bodies, and a tax on global financial transactions would be seen as supranational intervention; inferred, as sources do not mention it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Buchanan-style conservatives reject the race-based grievance narrative and are hostile to affirmative action, so they would say racism is no longer the main obstacle; inferred from the milieu.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The religious and cultural conservative allies of this current often hold natural-law views that an unjust law does not bind, but it is not documented in the sources; inferred and split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The anti-union, pro-work business current would doubt that society should aim to work far less, and Buchanan stressed jobs for American workers; this is inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Business nationalism opposes supranational bodies and defends sovereignty, and Buchanan's The Great Betrayal attacks a single globalist order, which fits several independent centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Business nationalists are laissez-faire, anti-communist capitalists, so they reject the Marxist labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Buchanan's economic nationalism argues that protecting American producers and workers goes with loyalty to the nation, and the current presents workers as victims of internationalist elites.

material-over-identity.rationale: The current allies with cultural conservatives and frames the fight as over elites, so a material-interests focus fits only partly; the statement is about the left and this is inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Business nationalism is anti-communist and anti-socialist, so it rejects a socialist system under communist rule outright.

missingStatements.text: Government should end all foreign aid.
missingStatements.rationale: Buchanan would end foreign aid completely, and the movement opposed foreign aid after the war.

missingStatements.text: Free trade agreements such as NAFTA and the WTO cost a country its manufacturing jobs.
missingStatements.rationale: Buchanan argues NAFTA turned a surplus with Mexico into a deficit and that the US loses millions of manufacturing jobs a year.

notes: Positions are those of the American business-nationalist mainstream; its nativist, racist and conspiracist factions would answer differently on race, immigration and minorities. Trump is listed in the source infobox but was not used for answers.
